note: LLM-authored analyst write-ups: outlook, ceiling/floor, projected role and team fit, grounded in draft_context.json signals (VOR, keeper-adjusted slot delta, handcuffs, keeper age/risk, news) plus football knowledge. Rendered by draft.js in place of recap().

teams.ddhk: Three every-week anchors in Christian McCaffrey, James Cook and CeeDee Lamb (~724 projected) give this roster the highest ceiling in the league — and a clear fault line. McCaffrey is still the engine at a projected 256, but he's 30 with a long injury history, which is exactly why the round-10 flier on Kaelon Black is the right kind of insurance rather than a wasted pick. Up top, Jaylen Waddle and rookie Luther Burden hand Lamb real support; Burden is a genuine breakout bet if the Bears' passing game takes the step his target projection implies, and Kyle Pitts is finally in a role that could unlock the athletic upside he's teased for years. The back half is a lottery of ceilings — MarShawn Lloyd went from bench stash to the Packers' lead back the moment Josh Jacobs landed on the exempt list, and rookies Emmett Johnson and Zachariah Branch are pure speed swings. Win-now floor, championship ceiling — health at running back decides which one shows up.
teams.danseung: The cleanest young core in the field: Ja'Marr Chase, Chase Brown and rookie Omarion Hampton (702 projected, nobody over 26), so there's no aging star to protect and no reason not to hunt upside. Garrett Wilson is a target monster who anchors an already-deep receiver room, and Quinshon Judkins profiles as a Year-1 workhorse if the touches land as projected. The quarterback plan is the smartest in the draft — Drake Maye (a projected 320 with 25 points of value over replacement) plus a last-pick Bo Nix stash means elite production for the price of a mid-round pick. Rookie Omar Cooper is the speculative WR ceiling swing. High floor, high ceiling, and zero glaring holes — the most complete build here.
teams.eikichii952: The richest keeper trio by projection — Josh Allen, Kenneth Walker and DeVonta Smith (776) — freed this roster to draft balanced and low-variance, and it did. Rookie Tetairoa McMillan brings real WR2 upside if the target share materializes, Cam Skattebo is a physical early-down back with goal-line value, and Joe Burrow at a projected 306 is almost unfair as a backup to Allen. Travis Kelce stabilizes tight end even in his decline. The one thing to track is Walker's murky situation this offseason — if his role slips, the RB room gets thin fast. But no reaches, no holes, and the safest week-to-week floor in the league.
teams.sathwikn: The Josh Jacobs exempt-list news guts this roster from the inside: Josh Jacobs is a kept back here, and with him out indefinitely and no handcuff drafted (Lloyd went to ddhk), a projected-186 cornerstone just vanished. Drake London and Breece Hall are strong when healthy, but Hall's carrying a Questionable tag, so the margin is thin. The draft leaned hard into upside — rookie Jeremiyah Love in the 1st has three-down bell-cow traits, TreVeyon Henderson could seize the early-down role in New England — and it landed the board's best value at tight end in Sam LaPorta (17 slots past the board, 32 points of VOR). Ceiling is real if the rookies hit; the Jacobs blow means this is the roster most reshaped by news.
teams.IconicJH: An elite spine in Jahmyr Gibbs, Chris Olave and Trey McBride (682), fronted by the receiver of the draft — A.J. Brown at a projected 207 and 70 points of value over replacement is a weekly WR1 ceiling. Terry McLaurin was clean value in the 2nd. From there it's a scattershot chase for a second running back — Kenny Gainwell, Jacory Croskey-Merritt and a Rachaad White handcuff on top of Croskey-Merritt — none with a locked role, which is where the reaches piled up. Mark Andrews is a sneaky bounce-back stash, but Zach Charbonnet is confirmed a reach: he's on PUP, out at least four games, with a rookie now in the mix. Star power at the top, a muddy backfield underneath.
teams.spiffster: Bijan Robinson and rookie phenom Ashton Jeanty give spiffster two projected bell-cows plus Nico Collins (724) — an enviable base. The round-8 Mike Washington pick handcuffs Jeanty directly, less an age play than insurance on a rookie whose projected workload cuts both ways. DJ Moore in the 1st looks like a 16-slot reach on the board, but he's a high-floor target hog whose volume rarely disappoints, and Mike Evans in the 3rd (49 VOR) was outright theft for a red-zone monster. Jaxson Dart is the swing-for-ceiling QB bet 26 slots late. Tank Dell is an IR stash, not a live contributor — he opens the year on injured reserve. Strong top, upside darts at the bottom.
teams.jonsung: A three-deep all-RB keeper base — Jonathan Taylor, David Montgomery and Travis Etienne (634) — that's stable at the position but pushed the draft toward receivers early, opening with Zay Flowers and D'Andre Swift (46 VOR) before landing George Kittle as a top-five tight end in the 5th. Jayden Daniels adds a rushing-QB floor that props up the whole lineup. Montgomery's age is a minor flag, but with three startable backs kept there was no need to reach for a handcuff. Deebo Samuel is a fit-dependent bet — his value hinges on how a new offense deploys him. Production-now with a slightly lower ceiling than the contenders above it.
teams.edgxrjiang: Puka Nacua is a bona fide WR1, but Ladd McConkey, Bucky Irving and Nacua himself are all carrying Questionable tags — an injury cloud over the entire keeper core (626). That context makes the early Bhayshul Tuten pick and its Chris Rodriguez handcuff a coherent play: build a stable backfield behind uncertainty. Tee Higgins (49 VOR) is a plug-and-play WR1, and Caleb Williams offers real dual-threat ceiling if the Bears' offense clicks. Matthew Stafford 68 slots past the board is the value of the draft at quarterback. The rookies in the middle (Nicholas Singleton, Kenyon Sadiq) were reaches. This roster's ceiling is a contender — if the keepers stay upright.
teams.Pkizzle3000: De'Von Achane (Questionable) and Saquon Barkley (29) are a high-end but fragile backfield alongside rookie TE Colston Loveland (631). The round-11 Jaylen Wright grab reads as a 71-slot reach, but as the Achane insurance on an already-dinged lead back it's defensible cover, not a blunder. The receiver bets up top are strong — Emeka Egbuka (48 VOR) and rookie Rome Odunze, who has a breakout profile if Chicago's targets consolidate — and Jalen Hurts gives a rushing-QB floor. Rookie QB Fernando Mendoza and Chris Bell are end-of-bench dice rolls. Boom-or-bust hinges entirely on the health of the Achane/Barkley pairing.
teams.andyxia124: Derrick Henry (238 projected at 32), Amon-Ra St. Brown and Brock Bowers headline (668), and Henry is the swing: still a top-tier producer, but at his age the cliff is real — and andyxia drafted no handcuff behind him, the roster's biggest single risk. Lamar Jackson in the 1st (326 projected, 30 VOR) is a cheat-code ceiling at quarterback and doubles down on a boom build. The receiver room is loaded (Jameson Williams, Brian Thomas, both ascending deep threats), but the mid-round RB darts (Tyjae Spears, Isiah Pacheco) went ahead of the board and none secures the Henry insurance this roster actually needs. Elite ceiling, thin margin if the 32-year-old breaks down.
teams.sallyyoon84: The lightest keeper haul in the league — Justin Jefferson, Kyren Williams and rookie Tyler Warren (557) — meant sallyyoon had to win the draft on value, and George Pickens (68 VOR, a projected 205) was a genuine coup with a clear path to target volume. Blake Corum is the logical Kyren Williams handcuff given the Rams' committee tendencies. The ceiling swing is two-way rookie Travis Hunter in the 13th — no bench holds a higher upside if the workload is real — and Brock Purdy 76 slots late makes quarterback a non-issue. Aggressive, upside-forward drafting to offset a thin head start.
teams.Paul_Yoon: An all-receiver keeper base — Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Malik Nabers (Questionable) and Rashee Rice — with genuine top-12 upside but zero kept running back, so the entire draft became a backfield-by-committee project: Javonte Williams, rookie Jadarian Price, J.K. Dobbins, Jonathon Brooks and a Jordan Mason/Demond Claiborne handcuff pair. Claiborne 86 slots ahead of the board is the biggest reach in the league on paper, but it's a deliberate ceiling bet on the Mason backfield rather than a misread. Dak Prescott 51 slots late is strong QB value. The receiver ceiling is real; whether one of the committee backs seizes a workhorse role is the season's swing question.
